name: UsageBar
intent: One bar for everything available in a period, split into the parts it is made of: what each part used, what is left, and anything spent past the allowance.
usage: Use UsageBar when a single allowance comes from more than one source and people need to see, in one line, where it went and how much is left — free credits, a plan and a top-up, say. It is one component: pass segments, each with an id, a value and a kind. kind "used" takes a chart intent and draws in that colour; kind "left" is the empty track and takes no intent; kind "outside" is what was spent past the allowance: it follows the last part of the allowance, draws red, and is not counted in what the bar measures. Its colour, its caption and its legend key say it is past the end, so nothing else marks where the allowance ran out. A segment with recent true draws as a darker sliver of the same intent right after its part, for the last hour, day or week. Each part can carry a label and a note, written under it as wide as the part; a part too narrow for its own caption leaves it out. figures writes up to three numbers above the bar — at "start", at "left" (the first part that is left) and at "end", right-aligned — each with a small line under it, and each able to take a warning or danger intent. The legend under the bar is the kit Legend, one key per used intent plus Left to use, keyed as an outline rather than a colour, and, when there is one, Over the allowance; turn it off with showLegend false. label names the bar for screen readers. Put it in a Section or Card, which gives it its title; the bar draws no box of its own. See contracts/usagebar.json for the full contract.

itemShape.value: number How much of the allowance this part is, in the same unit as every other part.
itemShape.kind: "used" | "left" | "outside"? What the part is. Default used.
itemShape.intent: green | olive | cyan | orange | pink | gray | purple | yellow | red | mint? The part's colour, on a used part only. Without it, used parts take the chart order.
itemShape.label: string? The bold line under the part, like Free credits or 670 left in the AI plan.
itemShape.note: string? The quieter line under the label, like 150 used · ran out Oct 12.
itemShape.recent: boolean? Draws the part as a darker sliver of its intent, for what was used in the last hour, day or week. Default false.
itemShape.legend: string? The name this part takes in the legend. Without it, parts of one intent share the first label, and the part that is left is keyed Left to use.

segments.note: The parts in the order they are drawn. Keep it short: two to eight, not counting recent slivers.

itemShape.value: string The big number, already written, like 1,170 or $156.00.
itemShape.label: string The small line under it, like left · 71% · lasts to the end of the period at this pace.
itemShape.at: "start" | "left" | "end" Where it sits: the start of the bar, the start of the first left part, or the end, right-aligned.
itemShape.intent: "warning" | "danger"? Colours the number amber or red, for an allowance running out or already past.

figures.note: Up to three, one per place. Leave it out for a bar with no figures above it.

showLegend.note: The kit Legend under the bar, centred. Turn it off where the captions already name every part.

label.note: Names the bar for screen readers, like Credits this period.

useWhen: An allowance that comes from more than one source — free credits, a plan, a top-up — and people need to see where it went in one line.
A usage or billing page where what is left matters as much as what is used, including use past the allowance.
A period view where each part needs its own caption, like when a part ran out or when the next one renews.
doNot: Do not use it for one limit with one number. Use Meter, or UsageList for several limits each with their own bar.
Do not use it to compare periods or trends. Use BarChart or LineChart.
Do not build it from a stacked BarChart with text under it, and do not add a local cousin like SegmentedBar or AllowanceBar.
Do not pass percents as values. Pass the real amounts; the bar works out the widths.
Do not count an outside part in the allowance. Pass it as kind outside and leave the used and left parts to add up to what was available.
Do not rely on colour alone: give every part worth naming a label, since the captions carry the meaning.
Do not put it in a Card and a Section at once, or draw a box round it yourself.
a11y: A group named by label, holding a meter whose text says how much of the allowance is used.
Every part is listed for screen readers with its label, note and amount, so the split is read in order and never left to colour.
The bar is not focusable: it shows a state and takes no input.
The legend is decorative here, since the captions already name the parts. Left to use is an outline key, so what is empty does not read as one more colour.
snippet:
<Section title="Credits this period">
  <UsageBar
    label="Credits this period"
    figures={[
      { value: "480", label: "used so far · 24 today so far", at: "start" },
      { value: "1,170", label: "left · 71% · lasts to the end of the period at this pace", at: "left" },
      { value: "1,650", label: "available", at: "end" },
    ]}
    segments={[
      { id: "free", value: 150, intent: "mint", label: "Free credits", note: "150 used · ran out Oct 12", legend: "Free credits" },
      { id: "plan", value: 330, intent: "purple", label: "AI plan", note: "330 used", legend: "AI plan" },
      { id: "plan-left", value: 670, kind: "left", label: "670 left in the AI plan", note: "renews Nov 9" },
      { id: "topup-left", value: 500, kind: "left", label: "500 left in the top-up", note: "no end date" },
    ]}
  />
</Section>

examples.title: Used and left
examples.usage: An allowance from two sources: free credits and the AI plan used, the rest of the plan and a top-up still to spend. The figures read used, left and available.

figures.label: used so far · 24 today so far
left · 71% · lasts to the end of the period at this pace

examples.title: Over the allowance
examples.usage: An outside part follows the allowance in red and is not counted in what the bar measures. The end figure takes danger, and the part still left takes warning.

examples.title: The last hour
examples.usage: recent draws a darker sliver of the same intent right after its part, for what went in the last hour. It is too narrow for a caption of its own.

figures.label: used so far · 11 in the last hour

examples.title: All used up
examples.usage: With nothing left to spend the figure at the start takes its own width: there is no part still to spend for it to line up with.

examples.title: One limit
examples.usage: A plain allowance from a single source, like API requests against a daily limit. One used part, one left part, and the gray intent where the bar is not about a coloured balance.

segments.label: 7,900 left today
segments.note: about 5,200 by the end of the day at this pace

examples.title: Without figures or legend
examples.usage: The bar and its captions on their own, for a panel whose numbers are already written above it.
